masthead_title: A Reader’s Guide to Thought, Freedom & Craft
prologue: “I put this guide together for close friends asking what shaped the way I think, build, and live. These aren’t books to pad a curriculum; they are high-leverage texts that provided me with mental clarity, discipline, and sovereignty. Read with a pencil, keep what serves you, ignore the rest.”
colophon_left: Marc Duboc · Reading Field Guide · Paris, France

books.title: Man’s Search for Meaning
books.author: Viktor E. Frankl
books.scenario: When feeling overwhelmed or losing your sense of purpose.
books.verdict: Frankl survived Auschwitz and distilled the ultimate truth: you cannot control all circumstances, but you retain absolute sovereignty over your attitude.
books.takeaway: Find a "why" strong enough to outlast the collapse of any "how."

books.title: Crépuscule
books.author: Juan Branco
books.scenario: Inspecting the revolving doors and inner circles of French power.
books.verdict: The internal mapping of Parisian elite networks and financial backing is documented with surgical precision. An unvarnished look at power.
books.takeaway: An unvarnished anatomy of institutional incest in modern France.

books.title: A Philosophy of Solitude
books.author: John Cowper Powys
books.scenario: Sinking into sensory calm during hyper-connected burnout.
books.verdict: Practical rituals—walking alone, observing wind and stone, deliberate silence—to build an unshakeable inner fortress against external noise.
books.takeaway: Cultivating your inner world is the only real shield against noise.

books.title: Promise at Dawn
books.author: Romain Gary
books.scenario: Rekindling fierce filial love, courage, and literary panache.
books.verdict: Gary’s unforgettable tribute to his mother’s boundless faith in him. Balances self-deprecating humor with extraordinary emotional gravity.
books.takeaway: The kind of book that makes you put it down and call your mother.
